about:
# Gold Wise

![Gold Wise](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flightpathlabs/GoldWise/main/docs/images/goldwise-banner.png)

An auction house helper for World of Warcraft: Forever. It looks at what
you're carrying, checks recent auction prices, and suggests whether to
sell, hold, vendor or keep each thing.

It doesn't post, buy or cancel anything for you, and there's nothing to
set up.

[Download](https://github.com/flightpathlabs/GoldWise/releases/latest) ·
[What's new](https://github.com/flightpathlabs/GoldWise/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) ·
[Report a problem](https://github.com/flightpathlabs/GoldWise/issues/new/choose)

## What's in it

- **Assets:** what you hold, with a price, a trend and a suggestion,
  and a watch list for anything else you want to keep an eye on.
- **Prospects:** pick a goal (gathering, crafting, reselling vendor
  recipes) and get a short plan.
- **Money:** whether you're coming out ahead, what's worth your time
  (gold an hour for what you do, profit on what you trade), and what's
  coming up, like training and repairs.
- **Recipes:** vendor recipes you haven't learned, and ones worth
  reselling.
- **Places:** the nearest trainer, bank, auction house and so on, with a
  map button.
- **Items:** any item's price history or crafting tree.
- **Session tracker:** a small panel showing what this play session has
  made.
- **Enemy values:** a creature's tooltip shows roughly what a kill is
  worth, learned from your own looting.

![The Assets tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flightpathlabs/GoldWise/main/docs/images/assets.png)

![The Recipes tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flightpathlabs/GoldWise/main/docs/images/recipes.png)

## Installing

Search for **Gold Wise** (with a space) in the CurseForge app, WowUp or
the Wago app. It's on
[CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/gold-wise) and
[Wago](https://addons.wago.io/addons/gold-wise).

To install by hand, download the `Goldwise-v...` zip from the newest
[release](https://github.com/flightpathlabs/GoldWise/releases) (not
"Source code") and unzip it into
`World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns\`.

## Getting started

Type `/gw` or click the minimap button, then visit an auction house once
so it can read prices. Opening your bank and profession windows once on
each character helps it know what you have.

| | |
|---|---|
| `/gw` | Open or close the window |
| `/gw history` | Price history for the item you last pointed at |
| `/gw tree` | Crafting tree for the item you last pointed at |
| `/gw goal 50` | Save toward 50 gold. `/gw goal off` clears it |
| `/gw session` | Show or hide the session tracker |
| `/gw report` | Gather what a bug report needs, ready to copy |

Right-click the minimap button for the options.

## Notes

- Prices come from your own auction house visits. Gold Wise players on
  the same market can share prices in game; you can turn that off.
- It works alongside Auctionator, Questie, Bagnon and others, and leaves
  out what they already show.
- Found a bug? Type `/gw report` in game and paste what it gives you into
  a [new issue](https://github.com/flightpathlabs/GoldWise/issues/new/choose).
  It includes no character names, realm or gold.

## For contributors

Work happens on `dev`; base pull requests there. `main` only moves at a
release. Changes go under "Unreleased" in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/flightpathlabs/GoldWise/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

```
Core/      startup, events, saved data, item names
Data/      tables: gathering, trainer prices, vendor recipes
Market/    which auction house, the request queue, scanners, price sharing
Ledger/    price storage and the sums over it
Profile/   what the player carries, banks, can make, and where things are
Advisor/   the rules that turn facts into advice
UI/        the window, tabs, charts, tooltips, cards and options
Media/     icon, portrait and artwork
```

Files load in the order in `Goldwise.toc`. Modules talk through the small
message bus in `Core/Events.lua`. On `dev`, `/gw demo` fills the screens
with invented figures for screenshots; release builds leave it out.
Formatting is StyLua and linting is luacheck.

## More from Flight Path Labs

Small addons for World of Warcraft: Forever, all at
[github.com/flightpathlabs](https://github.com/flightpathlabs).

- [Creel](https://github.com/flightpathlabs/Creel): a fishing log and one-key cast.
- [Temper](https://github.com/flightpathlabs/Temper): how your character fights, and whether a change helped. Coming soon.
- [Encore](https://github.com/flightpathlabs/Encore): helpers for enchanters. Coming soon.

## Licence

MIT. See [LICENSE](https://github.com/flightpathlabs/GoldWise/blob/main/LICENSE).

Class training prices and vendor recipes in `Data/` come from What's
Training? by Sveng, also MIT; details in [THIRD-PARTY.md](https://github.com/flightpathlabs/GoldWise/blob/main/THIRD-PARTY.md).
The goblin is an original cartoon; any resemblance to real people is
parody. Gold Wise is a fan-made addon, not affiliated with Blizzard
Entertainment.

  [![Flight Path Labs](docs/images/flight-path-labs.png)](https://github.com/flightpathlabs)

releases.name: Goldwise 0.6.0
releases.notes:
**New**

- **A Money tab in place of Purse and Profit.** One choice at the top
  (whose money, and this session, 7 days or 30 days), then three
  questions: are you making money, what's worth your time, and can you
  afford what's next.
- **What's worth your time.** Your play is split into what you were
  doing (killing a kind of creature somewhere, gathering, fishing,
  questing) with the time each took and what it brought in an hour. A
  second view shows each thing you traded: what it cost, what it brought
  in, and the profit.
- **Plainsight's nameplates** can show what a kill is worth, when
  Plainsight is installed.
- **The window remembers where you were:** it opens on the tab you last
  used, and the Money tab on the same character, period and view. It
  starts on your whole account over 30 days.

releases.name: Goldwise 0.5.1
releases.notes:
**New**

- **A watch list.** Right-click any item in Goldwise and choose Watch
  its price, or type `/gw watch` and shift-click one. Watched items
  have their own list on the Assets tab, with their price and trend,
  whether you hold any or not.
- **What you paid, against what it would bring in.** On the Assets
  tab, something you bought says what you paid each and whether
  selling it now would make or lose money.

**Fixed**

- **An enemy's worth no longer counts lucky drops as usual ones.** A
  green that dropped once in a handful of kills was counted as if it
  dropped that often, so a few creatures looked worth several times
  the rest. Greens and better now count at the rate they drop from
  everything of that kind and level, at a typical green's price, and
  show as one line, "Any green or better", on the enemy's tooltip.
- **Recipe profits allow for the deposit** as well as the auction
  house's cut.
- **Characters aren't listed twice.** When the game gave the realm's
  name as blank just after logging in, a character's records were kept
  apart from their own, and "Whose money" showed them twice. Those
  records are put back together, and the realm's name is remembered.
- **`/gw watch` with a shift-clicked item watches it,** rather than
  opening its price history. The same for `/gw tree`.

- **The session tracker shows your listings on their own line.** What
  you have up for auction was added into "At auction", so the bags
  looked worth far more than they held. It's now "Listed at auction",
  under the bags' own figures.
- **The recipe card's resale lines fit.** The vendor's name ran off the
  end of the line; it's on the row's map pin instead.
- **The recipe card keeps to its own zone.** Left up while you moved
  on, it could swap in the next zone's recipes under the old zone's
  name, and kept that zone's own card from coming up.
- **Buyouts are named more reliably.** A buyout the game couldn't
  price as you clicked was kept as a bid with no item, and the item
  could be put down to some other coin instead. Only purchases you
  asked for are named now, and a bid that was really a buyout becomes
  one.
- **Prices paid at vendors** are only noted once the coin has gone, so
  a purchase that failed doesn't count.
- **Older sales say what they cost without a profit,** as the deposit
  handed back with them wasn't kept and the figure would have been too
  high.
- **The Profit chart fits a day at a time** until auction trades kept by
  the hour cover what it would show, so the auction line isn't empty
  for the weeks before 0.5.0.
- **Looting no longer fills Goldwise's diagnostic log.** Only what's out
  of the ordinary is noted, once a session, so a bug report keeps the
  rest of what it needs.

releases.name: Goldwise 0.5.0
releases.notes:
**New**

- **Prices for other addons.** A small read-only `GoldwiseAPI` gives
  other addons the auction price Goldwise would show for an item, so
  Creel, the fishing log, can value catches without scanning the
  auction house itself. Other addons can also open Goldwise on an
  item's crafting tree or price history.
- **An Items tab, for finding anything.** Type part of a name, or
  shift-click an item into the box, and Goldwise lists what matches:
  what you carry first, then everything it has seen in your bags or at
  the auction house. Click one for its price history, or press its
  Crafting tree button. `/gw find` and a few words opens it from chat.
  To make that possible, Goldwise now remembers the names of items it
  has seen, for as long as it keeps their prices.
- **Right-click any item in Goldwise** for its crafting tree, its price
  history, or to link it in chat. It works on Assets, Profit's latest
  sales, Recipes, the plans on Prospects, the crafting tree's own rows
  and an item's page.
- **What an enemy is worth.** Point at a creature and its tooltip says
  roughly what one is worth to kill: its coin, its common drops with how
  often each falls and what it sells for, and what skinning it gives.
  Goldwise learns this from your own looting while you play alone, so
  it starts empty and fills in as you go. Until you've looted a few of
  something, it guesses from similar creatures and says so. An option
  puts a small coin and the figure above enemies' nameplates too; it
  starts switched off.
- **Recipes worth reselling, called out in town.** The recipe card
  that says a vendor nearby sells something you could learn now also
  points out recipes sold there that fetch a good deal more at auction
  than the vendor asks, whether or not you know them or have the
  profession. An option sets how much more counts, from a quarter more
  to triple, and the Prospects list of vendor recipes to resell goes by
  the same figure.
- **The Recipes tab in two columns.** Recipes to get, the ones you can
  use now first and closest to your skill, and potential sales, what's
  sold near you first and then by most profit. Each row has its own map
  pin for its vendor.
- **A log of your recipe resales.** Buy a recipe from a vendor that can
  be sold on, list it and sell it, and Goldwise keeps what it really
  cost, what it really sold for and the profit, deposits lost included.
  It's under Your resales on the Recipes tab.
- **Sort the Assets list** by sell value, by name, or by what Goldwise
  suggests doing with each thing. It remembers your choice.
- **The Profit chart fits what you've played.** Early on it shows the
  hours since your first coin, an hour at a time, and widens as your
  record grows until it shows the month a day at a time. A menu beside
  it picks a fixed span instead. Auction house trades are now kept by
  the hour for this, from this version on.
- **Sales say what they cost.** On the Profit tab, a sale of something
  you bought earlier, at auction or from a vendor, says what you paid
  and the profit left after it and the deposit.
- **What your bank would fetch.** While the bank is open, a strip over
  it says what your bank and the account bank would fetch, at auction
  and to vendors, and how many things in them are worth listing. It
  looks for the bank window of Bagnon and other bag addons too, and sits
  at the top of the screen when it can't find one. An option switches
  it off.

**Better**

- **The crafting tree knows all your characters' recipes.** It used to
  follow only the recipes of the character you're on, so a cloth
  robe your tailor alt makes had no tree on your main. Now each step
  says which of your characters can make it.
- **The session tracker can count your bank.** Tick Bank beside "Your
  bags, if sold" and it takes in your bank and the account bank as they
  were when you last had them open, so putting things in the bank no
  longer shows as a loss. It's off to begin with, and switching it
  doesn't restart the session.
- **The session tracker's "if sold" section is simpler.** It shows
  what your bags would fetch at auction and to vendors, and no longer
  the change since you started beside each, which read as a loss
  whenever you sold something. What you have up for auction now counts
  with your bags until it sells or its time runs out.
- **Goldwise's cards stay until you close them.** An option has them
  put themselves away after a while, as before. The recipe card has
  two sections, potential profit at auction and recipes you're
  missing, a map pin on each row for its own vendor, and a Don't show
  again button.
- **Alt-right-click always answers.** On an item none of your
  characters can make or use, it used to do nothing at all. It now
  opens the crafting tree page, which says so, and how Goldwise learns
  a recipe: open that profession's window once on the character who
  has it. The item's page always has its Crafting tree button too.

**Fixed**

- **Things bought at auction say what they were.** A purchase could be
  put on record as just "Bought at auction" when the game didn't have
  the auction's details to hand as you bought. It now takes the name
  the game gives once the purchase goes through.
- **The recipe card's map pins** were missing when it came up just
  after logging in, before Questie was ready.

releases.name: Goldwise 0.4.1
releases.notes:
**New**

- **Dismiss a recipe from the recipe card.** Each recipe on the "for
  sale here" card has a small X beside it. Click it and Goldwise stops
  mentioning that recipe; the card closes up and shows the next one. The
  recipe stays on the Recipes tab. The options page lists what you've
  dismissed and has a button to bring them all back.
- **A session tracker.** A small panel to keep on screen while you play,
  put there with the new Session tracker button on the Goldwise window's
  title bar, `/gw session`, or the options. It leads with what this
  session has made or lost in coin. Under that, where the coin came from
  and went: looted, quest rewards, sold to vendors, auction sales, and on
  the other side repairs, vendors, training, flights and the rest. Then
  what your bags would fetch if sold, at auction and to vendors, each with
  how far it has moved since the session began. Your bags aren't in the
  total, so something bought from a vendor shows as spent; the cog on the
  panel can count them in, and switches each section on or off. The arrow
  starts the session again, say before a run, and the button beside it
  folds the panel to a single line with the total. Click a line to open
  your purse or this character's assets. Drag it where you like;
  right-click to lock it. A reload, or logging back in within a quarter
  of an hour, carries on the same session. The pin in its corner opens
  Places, and pointing at it names the nearest auction house, repairs,
  bank, flight master and inn.
- **Goldwise's cards can be moved.** Drag the card that tells you about a
  recipe for sale nearby, or any other, to wherever you'd like them to
  appear, and they'll come up there from then on. Right-click one to put
  it back. The options have a button that puts one out to place. A card
  no longer puts itself away while you're pointing at it.
- **A cog for the options.** The Goldwise window has a settings cog
  beside its close button.
- **Any one character, or the whole account.** Purse and Profit now show
  the character you're playing, with a button beside each tab's menu to
  switch both to any of your other characters or to the whole account.
  Each character's own figures start from this version, so they fill in
  as you play, and an empty one says so; the whole account keeps
  everything it had. If you've only ever played one character with
  Goldwise, what they earned, spent and sold before carries straight
  over. Across the account, the latest sales name the character who
  made them.

**Better**

- **Purse tells more kinds of money apart.** Coin you loot, quest
  rewards and repairs are now kept apart from everything else, so the
  "mostly ..." line under spending can say repairs rather than "repairs
  and supplies". Earlier days stay as they were recorded.
- **A note on what's new.** The first time you open Goldwise after an
  update, a short note beside the window says what's changed, once.
  `/gw news` brings it back.

**Fixed**

- **Recipes are named on the recipe card.** A recipe the game hadn't
  fetched yet showed as "Recipe". It now shows the name of what it
  teaches straight away, and the recipe's own name once the game has it.
  The Recipes tab does the same.
- **Deposits that come back no longer count as spent.** When something
  sells, the auction house hands its deposit back in the sale's letter.
  Goldwise counted that letter as sold and kept the deposit as spending,
  so the Profit tab showed deposits as a cost after they'd been repaid.
  Now a sale's deposit comes off the deposits, and "Sold at auction" is
  what sales made after the cut. The profit figure was right before and
  hasn't changed. Sales from before this version stay as they were
  recorded.
- **"Make room" counts only your ordinary bags.** Empty slots in a
  quiver, ammo pouch or herb bag were counted as room for loot, so the
  reminder could stay quiet with your bags all but full.
- **"What materials are worth" keeps up.** It changed only after a read
  of the whole market. Prices from a search, the feed or other players
  now show there too, within half a minute.
- **Sharing a price over 214,000 gold**, as a joke listing might be, no
  longer goes wrong.
- "1 minutes ago" now reads "2 minutes ago".

releases.name: Goldwise 0.4.0
releases.notes:
**New**

- **The Purse chart can be cut finer.** A menu at the top of the tab
  sets how long a stretch each bar covers: a day, twelve hours, six, or
  one. Your choice is remembered.
- **Coin held, as a line.** The same menu swaps the bars for a line of
  what your characters held between them, stretch by stretch. It starts
  from this version: what you held before isn't on record.
- **An item's price within the day.** The price history page has a menu
  of its own: a point a day, as before, or every separate reading over
  the last week or the last two days. Prices that swing between morning
  and evening show up there. Goldwise keeps three times as many readings
  of each thing you hold as it did.
- **The verdict is on the tooltip.** Point at anything in your bags and
  Goldwise's line says Sell, Hold, Vendor or Keep, as the Assets tab
  would. It has a switch of its own in the options.
- **Auctionator's prices fill the gaps.** If you have Auctionator,
  Goldwise asks it, through the interface Auctionator offers other
  addons, for the last price of anything Goldwise has never priced
  itself: things Auctionator saw before Goldwise was installed, say.
  It's one price per item, so charts still fill in from your own visits,
  and the item's page says when a price is Auctionator's. Auctionator
  keeps one list for both factions, so its prices are only used for your
  own side's auction house, never over a price of Goldwise's own, and
  never passed on to other Goldwise players.
- **About lists the addons Goldwise works with**, and what it does
  differently beside each.
- **Point at the goblin in the corner of the window** and a tooltip says
  what Goldwise is, and which version you have.

**Better**

- **A day is now your day.** Goldwise counted days by the game's clock,
  which turns over in the middle of the afternoon in America and the
  middle of the morning in Australia. An evening's play and the next
  morning's landed on the same day, and the charts didn't move on. Days
  now run from midnight to midnight on your own clock, on every chart.
  Records from before the change sit a few hours out of place on their
  last day.
- **Every visit to the auction house counts, however short.** When
  Auctionator or Profession Atlas reads the market as you open the
  window, Goldwise reads along. It used to keep only the first 500
  prices unless that read ran to the end, so walking away after a few
  seconds left most of your things on their old price. It now keeps
  every page as it arrives. The same goes for Goldwise's own reads.
- **Fewer requests to the auction house when other addons are reading
  it.** When another addon asks for every auction, as Profession Atlas
  does, Goldwise now waits for that answer and uses it instead of reading
  the market itself at the same moment. If its own read is already under
  way when the list arrives, it stops. With Auctionator or Profession
  Atlas installed it also gives them a few seconds' head start on
  opening, so one read serves both.
- **Goldwise's tooltip lines say they're Goldwise's.** With several
  addons writing on the same tooltip, there was no telling which line
  was whose. Its line, the count your other characters hold, the
  crafting tree hint and the chart are now all marked with its name.
- **A price where the other addon has none.** Goldwise left tooltip
  prices to Auctionator whenever Auctionator was installed, so beside it
  there was often nothing of Goldwise's at all. It now asks whether
  Auctionator has a price for the item, and shows its own when it
  hasn't.
- **The tooltip chart appears after two days of prices**, not three.
- **Professions are recognised in any language.** They were matched by
  their English names, so on a German or French client Goldwise thought
  you had none. The rest of Goldwise is still in English.
- **A bid handed back is recognised in any language**, from the wording
  of the letter's subject, not only from the sender's English name.
- New releases reach Wago Addons as well as CurseForge.

**Fixed**

- **Roleplay-PvP worlds get a market of their own.** Their realm name
  ends in two words, and Goldwise read only the last, which filed their
  prices with the PvP worlds' and had the two swapping prices between
  players. If you play on one, your price history starts afresh under
  the right market.
